result.summary: Enables running the transaction index (-txindex) alongside block pruning (-prune), provided the index does not contain pre-v32 legacy entries. When a transaction lookup targets a pruned block, GetTransaction, REST, and RPC interfaces return the candidate block hashes instead of a generic not-found error. Callers can then download the missing blocks on demand via getblockfrompeer and retry, while getrawtransaction at verbosity 2 gracefully omits fee and prevout fields when undo data is absent.
result.problem: Nodes running in pruned mode cannot enable -txindex, forcing users who need raw transaction lookups, proof generation, or PSBT input resolution to maintain an unpruned node with hundreds of gigabytes of disk space.
evidence: PR description notes it resolves four long-standing issues requesting txindex support on pruned nodes: #10609 (opened in 2017), #12651, #16182, and #35240.
Builds on merged PR #35531, which restructured txindex records to map transactions to block hashes rather than direct disk file offsets.
result.scope_notes: Adds an optional data field to JSONRPCError, introduces src/node/tx_lookup_result.h, and changes the return type of node::GetTransaction from CTransactionRef to TxLookupResult.
result.changed_since_previous: Added a dedicated release note file (doc/release-notes-36002.md) and expanded test coverage for block undo data handling.
result.card: Allows Bitcoin Core nodes to run txindex concurrently with block pruning if the index contains no legacy file-offset entries. When looking up a transaction in a pruned block, txindex lookups surface the missing block hashes via REST and JSON-RPC error responses so callers can fetch them using getblockfrompeer and retry. Additionally, getrawtransaction at verbosity 2 omits fee and prevout data instead of failing when undo data is missing for refetched blocks. This addresses four issues dating back to 2017 (#10609, #12651, #16182, #35240) requesting pruned txindex functionality.

risk.why: Alters JSON-RPC and REST error structures and changes node::GetTransaction lookups across RPC and PSBT processing, which could break client integrations or cause lookup failures if block presence logic is flawed.
